title: Takedown containment: pool-scaled quorum, appeal path, suspension-before-permanence, revenue-scaled deposit (A10)
question: Do the registered repairs stop a thin-axis colluding set from irreversibly deleting a competitor for one vote round?

registered_notes.quorum: R-A10a: min_responders = max(floor, ceil(0.1 * pool)); floor 3 registered in SECURITY_FLOORS as takedown_min_responders
registered_notes.appeal: R-A10b: admissible only with at least one registered evidence class; judgement itself stays non-replayable
registered_notes.ladder: R-A10c: first ratification suspends 1 epoch; permanence only on re-ratification after the window

interpretation_registered_before_running.c1_fails: the quorum does not scale with the pool or dips below the floor - a thin axis can still force takedowns; VOID
interpretation_registered_before_running.c2_fails: appeals without evidence pass or cited evidence is rejected - the appeal path is either toothless or unbounded; VOID
interpretation_registered_before_running.c3_fails: first ratification delists or re-ratification cannot reach permanence - the ladder still lets one vote round delete a competitor; VOID
interpretation_registered_before_running.c4_fails: the deposit is flat or zero for valuable targets - deleting a valuable artifact stays cheap; VOID
interpretation_registered_before_running.all_hold: M315 PASS: takedown containment closes A10 at the registered cells
